nodes.prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 photo, the first frame of a video shot, looking like an ordinary frame from a real camera with a normal lens, not a render; true-to-life gentle colors and soft natural contrast; fine natural grain; the far background a touch softer than the foreground. No over-sharpening, no HDR, no CGI look. Image 1 is the empty birthday dining room: the shot takes place in exactly this room, same furniture, same light; keep the background exactly as in Image 1. Image 2 is the grandmother's character sheet: use it only for her face, skin tone, silver hair, glasses on the chain, jewelry and clothes. Image 3 is the granddaughter's character sheet: use it only for her face, skin tone, braids, earrings and clothes. Image 4 is her son's character sheet: use it only for his face, skin tone, haircut, beard and clothes. Image 5 shows the teal silicone utensils: use it only for their shape and teal color. Medium shot. The photo shows the grandmother walks around her birthday table carrying the potato salad bowl, a teal silicone serving spoon in her other hand; the granddaughter, seated right next to her father, has just pushed her plate away and grimaces, mouth open to speak; the rest of the Black American family, adults only, soft in the background. The grandmother: a 71-year-old Black American woman with medium-deep brown skin and warm undertones, a round face, short tapered silver-white coily hair, gold-framed reading glasses hanging on a chain at her chest, small gold earrings and a small gold cross. She wears a copper-colored silk blouse, a pearl necklace, a cream cardigan and a floral cotton apron. The granddaughter: a 19-year-old Black American woman with medium brown skin, long knotless braids gathered in a low ponytail, small gold hoop earrings and a bright, expressive face. She wears a plain grey hoodie with no logo and leggings. Her son: a 46-year-old Black American man with deep brown skin, a low taper fade with a little grey at the temples, a neatly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard, a tense jaw and a gold wedding band. He wears a navy quarter-zip pullover and chinos. The bowl is a large glass bowl of homemade potato salad (potatoes, chopped egg, celery, relish, a light dusting of paprika on top). Other dishes on the table, soft: collard greens, candied sweet potatoes and cornbread. Seating: her son on the right of the head of the table, the granddaughter right next to him, his wife across from them, two older Black American relatives at the far end. The granddaughter's own water bottle stands on the table at the far side of her place, away from her plate and her hands, and nobody touches it: a large light-pink insulated tumbler with a handle, a lid and a straw, plain, with no logo or lettering. Every hand has five fingers in natural proportion and a natural grip; each person has exactly two arms and two hands; nothing floats. Everyone's eyes stay off-lens; nobody looks into the camera. Look: warm evening light from a small chandelier, soft shadows, warm family-film color. Skin as a real camera sees it from a couple of meters away: natural, with subtle texture and slight unevenness, not retouched, not over-detailed; no airbrushed, waxy or plastic skin. Brown skin true to life: each person keeps their own skin depth and undertone, with soft natural highlights and visible detail in the shadows; palms lighter than the backs of the hands; never grey, ashy or lightened. Final check: the grandmother is the same woman as in her character sheet, with the same skin tone, silver hair, glasses on the chain and gold jewelry; the granddaughter is the same young woman as in her character sheet, with the same skin tone and braids; her son is the same man as in his character sheet, with the same skin tone, haircut and beard. No subtitles, no captions, no text overlays; the banner lettering in the background stays.

Medium shot, 6 seconds, one continuous shot, no cuts. The image is the start frame; the shot begins exactly on it. Camera: standing on a tripod, locked off, no movement. Physics: real weight and balance; nothing moves on its own: whatever moves is moved by a visible hand or by the action. Object lock: every utensil, bowl, plate, glass, brochure and prop in the picture is a rigid solid object that keeps exactly the same shape, size, length, color and number of pieces from the first frame to the last; nothing bends, stretches, melts, warps, splits, merges, multiplies, morphs or turns into something else; nothing appears, disappears or swaps places. Whatever anyone holds stays in exactly the same grip, length and angle as in the start frame and never slides through or passes through their fingers. People: everyone in the start frame keeps the same face, age, skin tone, hair and clothes; nobody is added or replaced; bodies move with real weight, feet on the floor. Action: The granddaughter says the line straight to her grandmother; the grandmother stops beside her with the bowl. Living layer (only what is already in the frame moves, nothing is added): the people breathe and blink naturally; anyone in the soft background breathes and shifts a little; a balloon ribbon in the frame sways slightly. Speech: the granddaughter speaks with clear lip-sync in the voice of a nineteen-year-old Black American college student: bright, casual, honest and direct, warm with her grandmother; natural, not an announcer, not salesy. This is the one voice used for the granddaughter in every clip of this video: keep exactly this voice, accent, age, pitch and pace. This time: blunt, honest, not mean. Exactly these words, word for word, nothing added or repeated: "Grandma, why does everything you make taste like SOAP?" The granddaughter starts speaking at about 0.4 seconds and has finished the whole line by about 4.0 seconds at the latest; after the last word she keeps the same feeling in her face, lips close and stay closed, no sound. Everyone else stays silent. Face: alive the whole time, never frozen, never a fixed smile; the expression follows the words through the brows, eyes and mouth corners; understated, never theatrical. Everyone's eyes stay off-lens; nobody looks into the camera. Real-time pace, nothing slow-motion; the main action starts within the first second. Keep the look, lighting and natural skin of the start frame to the last second. Audio: only the granddaughter's voice and quiet room tone of a family dining room, faint cutlery; no music. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text.
